- The previous experiment with high [S] and zero initial [P] successfully pushed M17 and M12 to the top, indicating that product-driven deactivation is highly likely. M14 and M20 are also plausible but lack P-dependence. M16 (substrate deactivation) dropped significantly.
- My aim was achieved: we separated the substrate-driven deactivation models from the product-driven and state-driven deactivation models. Now we must pinpoint exactly which catalyst state the product attacks, or if the deactivation is truly P-independent.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
To distinguish between M17 (P deactivates catS), M12 (P deactivates free cat), and M14/M20 (P-independent deactivation), I propose an experiment with maximum substrate ([S] = 5.0), high catalyst ([cat] = 0.15), and maximum initial product ([P] = 0.5). 
This condition directly contrasts with Run 3 by adding initial P, allowing us to isolate the effect of P on deactivation while maintaining a saturated catalyst state.
- For M17 (P + catS -> inactive): High [S] drives the catalyst almost entirely into the `catS` state. The high initial [P] will immediately and rapidly deactivate this abundant `catS` pool. The reaction will stall very early with minimal new product formed compared to Run 3.
- For M12 (P + cat -> inactive): High [S] minimizes free `cat` (a phenomenon known as substrate protection). Because the vulnerable free `cat` state is scarce, deactivation by P will be slow despite the high initial [P]. The reaction will proceed to a much higher conversion than M17.
- For M14 and M20 (catS -> inactive, etc.): Deactivation depends only on the catalyst states, not on [P]. The reaction progress (rate of S consumption) will be nearly identical to Run 3, showing no additional early stall from the presence of initial P.
- For M7: Lacks deactivation entirely and will proceed rapidly to full conversion, unaffected by P.
This single experiment perfectly separates the top candidates based on their unique responses to product inhibition under substrate-saturated conditions.
</hypothesis>
